name: Lyndon B. Johnson
summary: A New Deal-style Democrat who used the presidency to expand federal programs against poverty, for health care, schooling and civil rights, while backing a large military and an escalating war in Vietnam. He voted against civil rights bills early in his Senate career but later drove the 1957 and 1960 Acts and signed the 1964 and 1965 laws and the 1968 Fair Housing Act. He backed gun registration, liberal trade and foreign aid.

sources.usedFor: Senate record before 1957 (votes against anti-lynching, anti-poll-tax and FEPC bills), 1957 and 1960 Acts, Great Society legislation, Tonkin and Rolling Thunder, Immigration Act 1965, Public Broadcasting Act, Apollo

universal-healthcare.rationale: Signed Medicare and Medicaid (1965), giving state-guaranteed care to the elderly and the poor, and called it an insured right; he did not propose coverage for everyone, so the fit is partial.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Proposed extending the minimum wage to more than 2 million more workers (1964) and reported in 1967 that more than 9 million workers were now under a higher minimum wage; no claim that the rise was 'substantial'.

unions-good.rationale: Called labor an 'indispensable force in the American system' (1964) and asked Congress to repeal Taft-Hartley section 14(b) (1966).

cut-welfare.rationale: Expanded anti-poverty and social programs, vowed to 'accelerate and broaden' the attack on poverty, and wanted welfare redesigned to hold families together rather than cut.

limit-guns.rationale: Signed the 1968 Gun Control Act as the most comprehensive gun law to date and said it fell short: he had asked for national registration of all guns and licensing of gun carriers, which he said were needed.

empower-police-military.rationale: Called for an all-out effort against crime, pushed funding for police training and pay and signed the Safe Streets Act, and asked for the full $300 million for it in 1969.

decide-locally.rationale: Rejected 'purely local control over elections' and pressed national action on voting, civil rights and cities, though he spoke of 'creative federalism' with local leaders.

traditional-family.rationale: Called the family 'the cornerstone of our society' and urged policy to keep parents together.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Argued that freedom was not enough and that the next stage of civil rights was equality 'as a fact and as a result', with programs to overcome the legacy of slavery and oppression.

free-trade.rationale: Cited the Kennedy Round as the greatest tariff reduction in history and said America should maintain the liberal trade policies that made it the leading trading nation.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Pursued the Kennedy Round tariff reductions and 'liberal trade policies'.

military-superiority.rationale: Said US military power was 'strong enough to meet any threat and destroy any adversary' and that its superiority would keep growing while he held office.

equal-outcomes.rationale: At Howard he sought 'not just equality as a right and a theory but equality as a fact and equality as a result', while framing the goal as giving everyone the same chance; equal opportunity was 'essential, but not enough'.

limit-population.rationale: Offered help to nations trying to control population growth and said rapid population growth in developing countries must be slowed.

conscription.rationale: Maintained the draft through the Vietnam War, asked to modernise Selective Service and proposed a random-selection system in 1967 and 1969.

positive-liberty.rationale: Said 'freedom is not enough': citizens must have the ability to walk through the gates of opportunity, so he sought jobs, schooling, housing and health care.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Said 'men and women of all races are born with the same range of abilities' and that ability is stunted or stretched by family, neighborhood and school.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Mixed: pushed the 1964 tax cut as stimulus while aiming at a balanced budget, and in 1967 to 1968 asked for a tax increase to cut the Vietnam-era deficit.

force-without-un.rationale: Ordered air action and sought the Tonkin Gulf Resolution from Congress and committed ground forces in Vietnam without a UN Security Council authorisation.

class-collaboration.rationale: Urged business, labor and consumers to cooperate on price and wage restraint.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Signed the Civil Rights Act of 1964 barring racial discrimination in public accommodations, schools and employment, and guided the 1957 and 1960 bills through the Senate. His earlier votes against civil rights bills are superseded by this later position.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Defined freedom as the right to be treated 'as a person equal in dignity and promise to all others' and signed laws ending legal discrimination.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Described American justice as a nation where each man 'could be ruled by the common consent of all' and framed the voting rights bill around the democratic right to vote.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Declared a war on poverty and made ending poverty a central goal of his administration; the Economic Opportunity programs and Great Society targeted the poor.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Defended America's alliances and committed US forces abroad under them, saying the alliances are what 'the fighting' protects.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Pushed foreign aid aimed at hunger, disease and ignorance in countries that help themselves, called it the largest economic assistance program in the world, and renewed the food for freedom program.

collective-defense.rationale: Cited the SEATO treaty obligation 'to act to meet the common danger' of aggression as a reason for being in Vietnam and listed defence against Communist aggression in Korea, Formosa, Cuba and Vietnam.

character-from-environment.rationale: Said ability 'is not just the product of birth' but is shaped by family, neighborhood, school and surroundings.

space-expansion.rationale: As Senate majority leader and space committee chair he pushed the 1958 NASA act, and as president made the Apollo landing a national priority; 'central goal of civilization' goes beyond what he said.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Mixed: at Howard he said opportunity alone was not enough, but on signing the Civil Rights Act he said it 'does not give special treatment to any citizen'. He did not address admissions or hiring preferences directly.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Signed the Civil Rights Act of 1964 (public accommodations and employment) and the 1968 Fair Housing Act, and urged outlawing housing discrimination; his earlier opposition to civil rights bills is superseded.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: In the Great Society speech he wanted a society 'where men are more concerned with the quality of their goals than the quantity of their goods' and warned of a 'soulless wealth'.

non-intervention.rationale: Held that the US must resist outside aggression in Southeast Asia ('Hitherto shalt thou come, but no further') and intervened in Vietnam.

defeat-communism.rationale: Mixed: fought the war in Vietnam against Communist aggression and called Hanoi's aim a Communist takeover, yet pursued arms control, East-West trade and talks with the Soviets (Glassboro).

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Built up the armed forces and stressed military strength.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Led the Western bloc and fought in Vietnam as part of it.

racial-franchise.rationale: Drove the Voting Rights Act of 1965, striking down racial restrictions on voting in all elections.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Built Medicare, Medicaid, education and anti-poverty programs as government responsibilities rather than leaving the poor to charity.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Said the Great Society should meet the 'needs of the spirit' and build 'a richer life of mind and spirit'.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Contested: framed Vietnam as aiding a South Vietnamese government under attack, not as defence of US territory, and he escalated the war with bombing and ground forces.

future-generations.rationale: Called for a conservation effort to leave 'a green legacy for tomorrow' and warned that destroyed natural splendour can never be recaptured.

arms-reduction.rationale: Listed controlling, reducing and 'ultimately eliminating' the engines of destruction as a principle of policy and worked on non-proliferation, while raising military spending for Vietnam.

public-service-media.rationale: Signed the Public Broadcasting Act of 1967 to create non-commercial educational television.

farm-price-support.rationale: Wanted farmers to 'earn a fair reward' (1964) and in 1968 listed parity for farmers as an unachieved goal.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Asked Congress to repeal section 14(b) of Taft-Hartley, which lets states ban compulsory union membership, to equalise labor laws with the states that have no right-to-work measures.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Proposed a 'substantial cut in excise taxes' in 1964 to leave more money with consumers; those were taxes on selected goods and services rather than general sales taxes.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Mixed: the War on Poverty targeted the poor, while Medicare and education aid were broad programs for the elderly or all schools.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Named the heritage of slavery, oppression and 'present prejudice' as a main cause of Black poverty, alongside inherited poverty, and said the gap was widening 'despite the court orders and the laws'.

notes: Civil rights: he voted against anti-lynching, anti-poll-tax and fair employment bills as a congressman and senator (per Wikipedia), then helped pass the 1957 and 1960 Acts and, as president, signed the 1964 and 1965 acts and the 1968 Fair Housing Act; the later position is used. Vietnam: he escalated the war after the Tonkin Gulf Resolution (1964), defended it as resistance to Communist aggression, and on March 31, 1968 limited the bombing, offered talks and said he would not seek reelection.
